scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a consumer supplies newest-first or oldest-first entries
- **THEN** the timeline displays them in supplied DOM order and performs no independent date parsing or sorting
scenarios.name: Consumer chooses chronology
scenarios.requirementContent: Consumers SHALL own entry identity, ordering, chronology, timezone and locale formatting, audit semantics, filtering, pagination, persistence, permissions, live updates, announcements, and rerendering.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a consumer inserts labeled period groups
- **THEN** each label remains associated with its following entries and does not imply library-owned sorting
scenarios.id: data-display/history-timeline::Entry and grouping presentation::Entries span periods
scenarios.name: Entries span periods
scenarios.requirementContent: History Timeline SHALL support optional period labels, actor/avatar composition, multiline descriptions, metadata, attachments, current or emphasized entries, and empty or loading-safe presentation without embedding domain event names.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** entries contain long localized content or omit optional actor imagery and attachments
- **THEN** the timeline remains legible and does not render misleading empty affordances
scenarios.id: data-display/history-timeline::Entry and grouping presentation::Long and sparse entries
scenarios.name: Long and sparse entries
scenarios.requirementContent: History Timeline SHALL support optional period labels, actor/avatar composition, multiline descriptions, metadata, attachments, current or emphasized entries, and empty or loading-safe presentation without embedding domain event names.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** all required evidence levels pass with exact occurrences, supported limits, and consumer responsibilities recorded
- **THEN** History Timeline may move to `VERIFIED`
scenarios.id: data-display/history-timeline::History Timeline audit acceptance::Complete evidence permits verification
scenarios.name: Complete evidence permits verification
scenarios.requirementContent: History Timeline SHALL remain below `VERIFIED` until every occurrence is classified and source, structural, runtime-semantic, accessibility, focused visual, consumer, and responsive/content-stress evidence independently passes.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** an entry contains a consumer-authored attachment link
- **THEN** native activation and consumer logic determine the result
scenarios.id: data-display/history-timeline::Native consumer actions::Consumer opens an attachment
scenarios.name: Consumer opens an attachment
scenarios.requirementContent: History Timeline SHALL allow consumer-authored links and buttons but SHALL NOT filter, reorder, fetch, mutate, announce, or persist history.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the timeline is rendered at a narrow supported width with enlarged text
- **THEN** labels, entries, attachments, and actions reflow without clipping or changing semantic order
scenarios.name: Narrow timeline
scenarios.requirementContent: History Timeline SHALL preserve list order, connector continuity as decoration, visible focus, text scaling, and content reachability in narrow containers without page-level horizontal overflow.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a plain HTML or server-rendered consumer supplies documented timeline markup
- **THEN** entries remain readable in DOM order with actor, timestamp, and description relationships available without JavaScript
scenarios.id: data-display/history-timeline::Semantic history structure::Plain HTML renders history
scenarios.name: Plain HTML renders history
scenarios.requirementContent: History Timeline SHALL expose an accessible list of consumer-ordered entries with identifiable actor, timestamp, description, and optional metadata or attachments. Visual connector geometry MUST NOT replace list semantics or chronological labels.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a consumer replaces or appends message markup
- **THEN** the thread requires no undocumented library state to present the new content
scenarios.name: Consumer rerenders messages
scenarios.requirementContent: Consumers SHALL own message identity, ordering, author identity, sanitization, localization, delivery/read semantics, pagination, synchronization, persistence, moderation, attachment lifecycle, announcements, and rerendering.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a repository or built-DOM census finds an unclassified Message Thread occurrence
- **THEN** the occurrence guard fails and the module cannot be marked `VERIFIED`
scenarios.id: data-display/message-thread::Message Thread audit acceptance::Unclassified occurrence blocks verification
scenarios.name: Unclassified occurrence blocks verification
scenarios.requirementContent: Message Thread SHALL remain below `VERIFIED` until every occurrence is classified and source, structural, runtime-semantic, accessibility, focused visual, consumer, and responsive/content-stress evidence independently passes.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a message contains long localized text, links, unbroken content, or several attachments
- **THEN** content remains readable and contained without covering adjacent messages or causing page-level horizontal overflow
scenarios.id: data-display/message-thread::Message content and presentation states::Long localized content
scenarios.name: Long localized content
scenarios.requirementContent: Message items SHALL support incoming and outgoing alignment, consumer-authored body content, optional author/avatar, timestamp, metadata, attachment composition, grouped adjacency, and empty or loading-safe presentation. Direction and color MUST NOT be the only means of conveying authorship or state.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a message omits an avatar, attachments, or metadata
- **THEN** its remaining semantic content stays coherent without empty decorative placeholders
scenarios.id: data-display/message-thread::Message content and presentation states::Optional content is absent
scenarios.name: Optional content is absent
scenarios.requirementContent: Message items SHALL support incoming and outgoing alignment, consumer-authored body content, optional author/avatar, timestamp, metadata, attachment composition, grouped adjacency, and empty or loading-safe presentation. Direction and color MUST NOT be the only means of conveying authorship or state.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a message contains a consumer-authored action
- **THEN** native activation and consumer logic determine the result without a library event controller
scenarios.id: data-display/message-thread::Native consumer actions::Consumer handles an action
scenarios.name: Consumer handles an action
scenarios.requirementContent: Message Thread SHALL permit consumer-authored links and buttons while adding no send, edit, delete, retry, reaction, delivery, read-state, or navigation behavior.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** the thread is rendered in a narrow container with enlarged text
- **THEN** messages reflow within the container and all controls and attachments remain reachable
scenarios.name: Narrow container
scenarios.requirementContent: Message Thread SHALL preserve DOM reading order, visible focus, text scaling, and content reachability from narrow containers through supported desktop widths.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a consumer renders the thread
- **THEN** navigation, filters, profile panels, synchronization, and compose controls are not required by its interface
scenarios.id: data-display/message-thread::Semantic thread and message structure::Application shell is omitted
scenarios.name: Application shell is omitted
scenarios.requirementContent: Message Thread SHALL expose an accessible ordered or unordered message list whose items preserve author, timestamp, body, attachment, and metadata relationships without requiring an application shell.

scenarios.content:
- **WHEN** a plain HTML or server-rendered consumer supplies documented thread markup
- **THEN** messages remain readable in source order with identifiable authors and timestamps without JavaScript
scenarios.id: data-display/message-thread::Semantic thread and message structure::Plain HTML renders a thread
scenarios.name: Plain HTML renders a thread
scenarios.requirementContent: Message Thread SHALL expose an accessible ordered or unordered message list whose items preserve author, timestamp, body, attachment, and metadata relationships without requiring an application shell.
